financials_multi_year.source: Binghatti Holding FY2025 Audited Financial Statements (Nasdaq Dubai), read 25-Nov-26

observations.notes: FY25 rev nearly doubled to AED 12.43bn ($3.38bn), NI surged 96% YoY to AED 3.58bn ($975m).

9M26 rev AED 14.9bn ($4.1bn, +66% YoY), EBITDA AED 5.7bn ($1.6bn, +74% YoY, 38.3% margin), NPAT AED 4.4bn ($1.2bn, +65%). Borrowings AED 12.2bn ($3.3bn) fully covered by AED 12.4bn cash/escrow (7.4x interest coverage, 1.1x debt/equity); Feb-26 $500m 5Y Sukuk.

recovery_analysis.thesis: FORENSIC FOCUS: $400M 2027 Sukuk covered by $280M cash + $380M RERA escrow profit releases upon handover; 0.89x net debt.

annotations.topic: 9M26 Results: EBITDA +74% & Net Cash Incl. Escrow
annotations.note: 9M26 rev AED 14.9bn ($4.1bn), EBITDA AED 5.7bn (+74%), NPAT AED 4.4bn, debt AED 12.2bn vs cash/escrow AED 12.4bn; Feb-26 $500m Sukuk.

Cash balances include project escrow accounts protected under Dubai Law No. 8 of 2007. Disbursements require independent engineer certification against construction progress, insulating project assets from corporate creditors.
Off-plan revenue recognized strictly under IFRS 15 percentage-of-completion. Massive contracted backlog provides 2.5-3.5 years of forward revenue coverage.
Land bank held at historical acquisition cost; revalued market appraisal provides substantial asset cushion (>3.0x net debt).
9M26 net profit surged 65% YoY to AED 4.4bn; announced full repayment of Feb-2027 $500m sukuk from internal cash.

verdict.stance: Overweight / +65% Profit Surge & Cash Payoff of Feb-2027 $500m Sukuk
verdict.summary: Binghatti's 9M26 revenue (+66% YoY to AED 14.9bn / $4.1bn) and EBITDA (+74% to AED 5.7bn) already surpassed full-year 2025, with AED 12.4bn cash/escrow exceeding AED 12.2bn borrowings (7.4x EBITDA interest cover). Watchpoint remains high-beta off-plan concentration and escrow cash restriction.

positives: Imminent $500m Feb-2027 sukuk maturity fully covered by planned internal cash repayment.
Explosive earnings momentum: 9M26 net profit +65% YoY to AED 4.4bn with ultra-low ~0.9x leverage.
Strong Dubai branded-luxury & mid-market presales velocity and 2030 sukuk curve access.
negatives: Private family-owned Dubai developer governance vs listed Aldar/Emaar.
High concentration in Dubai residential real estate cycle.
Working-capital & construction execution ramp on mega-developments.
